clue.text: He does not give a Scottish doctor's surname

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
Ian is a typical Scottish forename, the Scots form of John

explanation.surface: A remark that someone declines to reveal what a Scottish physician is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue comments on the result: A, DR and the Scottish name IAN make a man's first name, so it does not give the doctor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The result is a man's given name, so it can stand for a male person, 'he'.

clue.text: Applauds article with many objects

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
CCL is 250 in Roman numerals, standing for a large number
objects as in goals, aims

explanation.surface: Someone praises a piece of writing full of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'objects' means goals, not things; 'many' is a large Roman numeral, CCL = 250.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to praise loudly and publicly.

clue.text: A sign to a quiet worker to become aggressive

parts.note: the Ram, Aries, is a sign of the zodiac
p, piano, is the musical instruction for quiet
a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A gesture to a silent labourer to get rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' means a zodiac sign, the Ram (Aries).
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained and violent, as aggression is; in heraldry a rampant beast rears up to attack.

clue.text: Milton's shady wench has Naroissus in her family

definitions.meaning: in Milton's Lycidas a shepherd might 'sport with' this girl 'in the shade'
a lily-like flower of the family that also includes the daffodil genus Narcissus

explanation.surface: A poet's girl in the shadows is related to the vain youth of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a pastoral girl's name in Lycidas and a bulb plant in the same botanical family as daffodils.

clue.text: The Speaker and I love church music

parts.note: a speaker who addresses an audience is an orator
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A parliamentary Speaker and the narrator share a fondness for sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Speaker' suggests the presiding officer of the Commons, but it is just a public speaker. Love = O comes from the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended musical setting of a sacred text for voices and orchestra, performed in churches and concert halls.

clue.text: Thirst gave Rita convulsions but she's OK now

indicators.note: convulsions are violent spasms, signalling the three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Rita had fits from thirst but has recovered now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convulsions' rearranges the letters of THIRST GAVE RITA. A trivet is a three-legged stand, proverbially steady.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old idiom for being perfectly well and in good order, i.e. fine.

clue.text: We have to know the sign

parts.note: ken is an old and Scottish verb meaning to know

explanation.surface: A statement that we must recognise the signal.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN, to know, is Scots and archaic English.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is an outward mark or symbol of something, a sign.

clue.text: Sapper changes daily, unlike Ethelred

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer, of the Royal Engineers, RE

indicators.note: changes says the letters of daily are altered in order

explanation.surface: A soldier alters his daily routine, unlike an old English king.
explanation.walkthrough: Ethelred was 'the Unready', so 'unlike Ethelred' means ready, willingly; 'changes' is the anagram signal for daily, after the Royal Engineers soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was never prepared; unlike him means doing things promptly and willingly.

clue.text: Vast amounts? Actually only five

parts.note: vast amounts reads as heaps of something, but the great bodies of salt water are traditionally counted as five

explanation.definitionFit: The plural word means huge quantities colloquially, and the world's great seas are counted as five: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, Southern.

clue.text: Hamlet's madness took such bearing

parts.note: Hamlet says he is but mad in one compass direction, a bearing just off north towards the west, and sane when the wind is southerly

explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing between north and north-west, the direction Hamlet gives his feigned madness.

clue.text: Join us for food in the wild Congo

indicators.note: the word for food is set inside the scrambled letters of the river name
wild suggests letters running out of control, so Congo is rearranged

parts.note: a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and eat somewhere in the untamed Congo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join us' is the definition, an invitation; 'wild' scrambles the river name and 'in' places the meal inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation phrase urging someone to accompany the speakers, much as 'join us' does.

clue.text: At the King's Head the Welshman's back, the rogue

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so the first letter of King is taken
back means the name of the Welshman is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Evan is a stock Welsh forename, so a Welshman in crosswords is often EVAN

explanation.surface: In a pub called the King's Head a Welsh scoundrel has returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head sounds like a pub name. Take K from the head of King, then 'back' turns EVAN into NAVE; the 's of Welshman's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest man, a scoundrel, which is what a rogue is.

clue.text: Probing your mind gets him any-way about a pound

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: taken as written
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound
ST, for street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road

explanation.surface: Someone who probes the mind, perhaps reached in any way at the cost of a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'any-way' hides a break between two pieces. The definition describes a psychoanalyst, the one you get to probe your mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychoanalyst explores a patient's thoughts and feelings, so this is the professional you engage to probe your mind.

clue.text: It's shockingly high

parts.note: the high voltage carried by power lines gives an electric shock, and also strain or suspense running high

explanation.definitionFit: Electrical potential, as in high-voltage cables, gives shocks; the word also means nervous strain, which can run high.

clue.text: Doctor allowed to go back to the lodging

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a military doctor

indicators.note: to go back means the word for allowed is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to allow, so allowed gives let

explanation.surface: A physician permitted to return to where he is staying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' reverses the word for allowed; MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motel is a roadside hotel offering rooms for travellers, a form of lodging.

clue.text: Prominent features about a poet getting bouquets

indicators.note: about means the facial features are placed around the poet

parts.note: noses stick out from the face, so they are prominent features
John Gay, author of The Beggar's Opera, is the poet

explanation.surface: Big noses around a versifier who is being presented with flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is John Gay, of The Beggar's Opera; 'about' has the noses enclosing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bunches of fragrant flowers, posies, are the same thing as small bouquets.

clue.text: Low joints-here's how to get the angle.

definitions.text: Low joints-here's how to get the angle.

parts.words: Low joints-here's how to get the angle.
parts.note: bending the knee low in worship; the word is Latin for knee plus bend, so the knee joints make the angle

explanation.definitionFit: To bend one knee to the ground in reverence, as in church.

clue.text: Kipling bracketed them with lesser breeds

definitions.text: Kipling bracketed them with lesser breeds

parts.words: Kipling bracketed them with lesser breeds
parts.note: in Kipling's Recessional, 'such boastings as' these people use are paired with 'lesser breeds without the Law'

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical word for non-Jewish peoples, heathens, which Kipling sets beside 'lesser breeds' in Recessional.

clue.text: The bit about the prows perhaps ? Yes

definitions.text: The bit about the prows perhaps ? Yes

indicators.note: about tells us the small piece wraps round the rearranged ship word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of prows may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A question whether this is the part around a ship's prow, answered in the affirmative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' scrambles the ship word and 'about' wraps the bit round it. Read whole, the clue also describes the spar at a ship's prow, and 'Yes' confirms that reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar projecting forward from a vessel's stem, so a part sticking out at the front of the prow.

clue.text: Gets round disposal units about the army

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: about means the rubbish containers go round the army

parts.note: bins are units for disposing of rubbish
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier collects rubbish bins around the barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'about' has the bins enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire or get hold of it.

clue.text: Alias Mrs White in an oyster-shell ?

definitions.text: Alias Mrs White in an oyster-shell ?

parts.words: Alias Mrs White in an oyster-shell ?
parts.note: Mrs White is a mother and white is pearl, so the alias is the other name for mother-of-pearl, the lustrous lining of an oyster-shell

explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining of oyster shells, has this other name.

clue.text: Sounds a tricky animal

indicators.note: sounds means the answer is said like a word for a tricky person

parts.note: a tricky person is a cheater, a swindler

explanation.surface: A creature that seems crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the big cat and 'cheater' sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest land mammal, a spotted big cat of Africa.

clue.text: Reserved-as a road-hog should be!

definitions.meaning: held in advance, as a table or seat
a reckless driver ought to be charged by the police, named in the officer's notebook

explanation.surface: A complaint that a reckless motorist ought to be held to account.
explanation.definitionFit: Booked means held in advance and also cautioned or charged by a police officer.

clue.text: Good man in the choir maybe gets the bird

indicators.note: the good man is placed inside the rearranged choir
maybe suggests the letters of choir could appear in another order

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous chorister ends up getting the bird, meaning booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' suggests being jeered, but the bird is the definition; 'maybe' scrambles the choir and 'in' sets the saint inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless African bird, the fastest-running bird alive.

clue.text: Goddess raises a point in anger

indicators.note: in places the point inside the word for anger

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

indicators.note: raises in a down clue lifts the letters, reading them upwards, so backwards

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A deity makes an argument while furious.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raises' means reading upwards, so the compass point is turned before 'in' sets it inside the anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Eirene was the Greek personification of peace, one of the Horae.

clue.text: To alter cases, modulate your voice

definitions.meaning: in grammar, to change a word's ending for case, number or tense
to vary the pitch or tone of speech

explanation.surface: Advice to change grammatical endings and vary your tone when speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers grammatical change of word endings and also varying vocal pitch; both are bending of form.

clue.text: "Where the wind's like a whetted" (Masefield)

parts.note: a fill-in from John Masefield's poem Sea Fever: the missing last word is the sharpened blade the gale is compared to

explanation.definitionFit: A whetted object is one sharpened on a stone, and the word completing Masefield's line is a bladed tool.

clue.text: Natural spirit of the French people in a late return

indicators.note: in puts the French article and the people inside the turned word
return means the word late is read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the
men is a common word for people

explanation.surface: A nature spirit among French folk who came back late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses late, and 'in' sets the French article and the people inside it; an elemental is a folklore spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore an elemental is a spirit embodying one of the four elements of nature, such as a sylph or salamander.

clue.text: How 12 examines girl's schools

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana; with the possessive it gives DIS
schools of thought or belief are sects

explanation.surface: How an analyst looks into the schools a young woman attended.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is ANALYST, who examines things by cutting them apart; 'schools' means schools of thought, not places of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Analysis breaks a subject into parts, and cutting something up to study it is exactly what an analyst does.

clue.text: Engraves a piece from a pocket chess set

indicators.note: a piece taken from the words pocket chess is a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone carves a figure from a travel chess set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a piece from' points to the run of letters spanning pocket and chess; 'piece' also tempts as a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving and this verb both mean cutting a design into a hard surface, often with acid.
